name: modifier-expressions
title: Expressions in layout modifiers
summary: A download card where layout modifiers take expressions: the bar is fillMaxWidth(@p), the percent bubble is offset by clamp(0, 280, @p * 328 − 24), equalizer bars get height from an array, and the caption fades with graphicsLayer alpha.
prompt: A download progress card: a bar filled to the progress, a percentage bubble that rides above the end of the bar, a row of level bars, and a caption that fades in as progress grows.
teaches: Pass an expression to a size modifier: {"fillMaxWidth": "@p"} fills that fraction of the parent, {"height": "10 + 54 * arrayGet(@eq, k)"} sets pixels
Move a component with {"offset": {"x": expr, "y": 0}}, clamping the expression so it stays inside its box
pitfalls: spacedBy parses an expression but the layouts keep it as a constant: "spacedBy": "@gap" writes a variable id that is used as a number (NaN), and the children lose their positions. Use constant spacing
Padding takes an expression only in its single-number form ({"padding": "@pad"}); the list and object forms are read as constants
fillMaxWidth's fraction is of the parent's width after its padding; the bubble's offset is in pixels, so it multiplies by the track width (328) itself

Inside a modifier, componentWidth() is the width of the component being modified (the 48 dp bubble), not of its parent: for a position along the parent, derive it from windowWidth() minus the padding, or a weight/fraction
Ten 22 dp bars with 8 dp gaps overflow a narrower host: give each bar weight 1 with widthIn [0, 30] and an end padding for the gap, so they shrink but never grow past the design

snippets.note: offset x = clamp(0, windowWidth() - 80, @p * (windowWidth() - 32) - 24): the bubble follows the bar end at any width (the bar spans the window minus the 16 dp padding each side)

check.describe: The blue bar is filled to 65 % with a 65 % bubble centred over its end, ten purple bars of different heights below, and a dimmed caption. Resized, the bubble stays centred over the bar end (65 % of the live width), and the ten bars share the row (weight 1, at most 30 dp each with an 8 dp end padding as the gap): thinner at 234 wide, as at 360 when wider.
